title: Componentwise naturality of currying
statement: For a site (C,J), a sheaf R of commutative rings, cochain complexes K,K',L,L',M,M' of R-module sheaves, cochain maps f : K' → K, g : L' → L and h : M → M', and integers n,p,q with p+n=q, let A be the degree-n map induced by f,g,h from Hom(K,Hom(L,M)) to Hom(K',Hom(L',M')). Let B be the degree-n map induced by the total tensor map f⊗g and h from Hom(Tot(K⊗L),M) to Hom(Tot(K'⊗L'),M'). Let c and c' be the chosen degreewise currying maps for (K,L,M) and (K',L',M'), and π' the (p,q) product projection of the latter target Hom term. Then (A ≫ c') ≫ π' = (c ≫ B) ≫ π'. Only this fixed projection is asserted; equality of the maps into the full product is proved separately.

proof.text: Eliminate the equality p+n=q and apply homTensorLocalized_ext to the two displayed projected composites. It suffices to compare their values on every localized pure tensor of each (i,j) summand with i+j=p.

For each summand substitute p=i+j. Apply homTensorCurry_natural_pure to the two chosen degreewise maps. Their hypotheses are the first components of homTensorDegreewiseMap_spec for the unprimed and primed triples. This proves all the pointwise equalities required by the extensionality lemma.

            (op (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K' L' (curriedTensor Mod)))).map h).f n) ≫
